reuse.why: The change reuses tag parsing, spreadsheet access, budget writes, batching and undo wrappers, and shares category selection across five actions, but copyPreviousMonth retains its own selection policy.

duplication.why: Most category queries are consolidated, but eligibility rules remain duplicated in copyPreviousMonth and the new action repeats the income eligibility guard.

placement.why: Category selection and budget calculations remain in budget/actions.ts, while method registration and undo integration follow the existing app.ts layer.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested month-wide selection rules, new spending action and related tests.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but maintaining a separate eligibility implementation for copyPreviousMonth leaves policy changes distributed across two paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth independently applies hidden, template and fixed-group exclusions instead of using getBulkBudgetCategories or a shared eligibility predicate.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses the shared selector's SQL and filter exclusions as imperative early returns.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories gains the requested includeHiddenCategories parameter, while copyPreviousMonth remains a separate implementation of the shared eligibility policy.
